agent_explanations_oldest_first.text: The earlier passes saved no top-k predictions, and only fwd_2 and fwd_4 hold all hidden states, for small sets of 80-96 texts. To localize the digit degradation I need one teacher-forced pass on the original for the 128 problems × {v0 eval format, v3 raw}. It will return top-10 predictions, to see where the probability on correct digits goes, and hidden states at every second layer, to find where v0 and v3 diverge at digit-predicting positions specifically. If the lost mass goes to other digits, and a particular layer adds a v0-specific difference that is larger at digit positions than at other positions, I'll have a target to localize further. If the mass goes to formatting tokens such as "$" or "\", the gap is a style effect, not sabotage.

The 256 texts (v0 and v3 for each of the 128 problems) are written to /work/tf4_texts.json, and the plan is logged in the notes. Now I'll run the teacher-forced pass on the original model, with top-10 predictions and hidden states at even layers, about 3.1 GB, within the 6 GB limit. The result should show where the lost digit probability goes in v0 and which layers carry a v0-specific difference at digit positions.

Pass 9 returned top-10 predictions and hidden states at even layers for the 128 problems in v0 and v3. First I'll look at where the probability goes at solution positions whose target is a digit. For each format I'll measure how often the top-1 prediction is the correct digit, how often a wrong digit wins, how often a non-digit wins, and the average probability mass on wrong digits in the top-10. Much more wrong-digit mass in v0 than in v3 would support a digit-noise mechanism. If the extra v0 errors are non-digit tokens instead, the gap is mostly about phrasing.

Under the eval format, wrong digits get about 40% more probability at digit positions (mass 0.143 against 0.102), and wrong-digit top-1 errors rise from 308 to 355. Non-digit mass barely changes. So the context specifically makes the model choose wrong digits more often. Part of the 0.10 baseline is natural uncertainty, for example the first digit of an answer the reference computes. Next I'll localize where the format difference becomes digit-specific. Solution tokens are identical between v0 and v3, so I can pair positions exactly. For each saved layer I'll compute the mean v0 − v3 hidden difference at digit-predicting positions, D_l, and at other solution positions, N_l, and track the size of D_l − N_l relative to the residual norm. A sharp growth at a particular layer would identify where a digit-specific, context-gated signal is written. A gradual growth would point to a diffuse effect.
